I-001.threat: Process data leakage — sensitive data processed by the process is exposed
I-001.cause: Process outputs or error messages contain sensitive information — no output filtering applied
I-001.attack: Attacker observes process output and extracts sensitive configuration data, credentials, or business information

I-002.threat: Process memory disclosure — attacker reads sensitive data from process memory
I-002.cause: Process memory is accessible without authorization — debug interfaces not disabled
I-002.attack: Attacker uses debug interface to read process memory and extract cryptographic keys or credentials

I-003.threat: Data flow eavesdropping — attacker intercepts sensitive data on the data flow
I-003.cause: Data flow is unencrypted — sensitive payload is transmitted in plaintext
I-003.attack: Attacker passively monitors the data flow and captures sensitive data

I-004.threat: Data flow metadata disclosure — attacker infers sensitive information from traffic patterns
I-004.cause: No traffic obfuscation — timing and volume of data flows reveal sensitive operational information
I-004.attack: Attacker analyzes data flow metadata to infer sensitive operational state

I-005.threat: Data store information disclosure — attacker reads sensitive data from the data store
I-005.cause: Data store lacks encryption or access control — data is stored in plaintext
I-005.attack: Attacker gains read access to the data store and extracts sensitive configuration or credentials

I-006.threat: Data store backup disclosure — sensitive data exposed through unprotected backup
I-006.cause: Backup files are not encrypted or access-controlled
I-006.attack: Attacker accesses backup files and extracts sensitive data without compromising the primary store
